title: Financial Management & Essential Needs
privacy: Public register omits addresses, DOB, government/customer references, bank details, card identifiers, login/security data and unrelated third-party private information.
legalStatus: Public evidence register; not a court finding of unlawful conduct.

records.summary: Onboarding stated that TAG would prepare a budget and pay bills.
Allowance documented as $360/week: Tue 40, Wed 40, Thu 200, Fri 40, Sat 40.
Customer disclosed gambling loss affecting allowance and phone money.
Customer disclosed continuing gambling and proposed smaller regular payments; TAG response showed direct board/rent payment mechanism where payee details could be established.
TAG said allocated funds would need to be used by customer to pay rent.
Customer reported gambling every cent and asked TAG to pay rent using his money.
One-off $175 accommodation payment; direct-payment option offered if park payment details could be arranged.
Direct rent + pharmacy/health + phone + five equal daily living shares + one savings share proposed in writing.
Services Australia screen shows net $1,252.42, compared with $1,150.90 on several earlier fortnights.
Customer asked TAG to stop giving unrestricted money after another gambling loss and to pay rent.
TAG listed Tue 80, Wed 70, Thu 200, Fri 80, Sat 80; stated total allowances $1,050, phone $27, remainder $73. Listed daily figures equal $510/week; if weekly, $1,020/fortnight.
Customer reports Friday $160 and Saturday $80 lost entirely online, no money used for essentials, rent arrears around $100-$150 and no money for food.

exclusions: No claim that NSW Trustee & Guardian has been judicially found to have acted unlawfully.
No claim that any money is proven missing.
No claim that the caravan park is proven to have committed tax evasion or another offence.
No unverified observation about an individual is presented as established fact.
